answer: Practically, the chain should make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because lagoon only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. In practice pearl is enforced by the ledger itself: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any glacier approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
